newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish money market tight, seen dry until yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Polish money market tight, seen dry until yr-end.

text.p: The Polish money market is seen remaining underliquid until the end of next week and some dealers expect the cash-shortage, caused by fast credit growth in recent months, to hold until 1997.

On Tuesday, deposits again traded around the 25 percent lombard rate, some six percentage points higher than at the end of November, as banks felt the squeeze of large credit outflows coupled with pre-Christmas spending outflows.
"It seems rates could stay around present levels until the end of the year...unless the central bank offers a repo operation, which is unlikely," said Robert Kulak of Pekao SA.

Some dealers said the market could regain some liquidity at the end of next week as banks, which have been building up required reserves from the start of the month, start placing surplusses on the market.

They said the crucial day for the money market will be next Friday, December 20, because if rates fall on that day it could signal that banks have surplusses and that rates would not return to lombard levels for the rest of 1996.
Overnight and tomorrow/next closed flat at 24.80/25.05 and 24.85/25.05 percent respectively, while two-week depos at 24.0/25.0 against the last 14-day drainage rate of 19.16.
Low liquidity on the money market also stired up demand for zlotys on the forex market, pushing the zloty up to 2.78/2.72 percent from the trading band centre from 2.74/2.68 percent on Friday.
"The zloty should trade at these levels (2.7 percent from parity) for some time to come as demand for zlotys is likely to remain high," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 2.8580/90 per dollar, down from 2.8410/30 after the dollar's rise to above 1.55 marks on world markets, and at 1.8416/25 to the mark, up from 1.8554/63.
